title: Psalm 98: Victory, Music, and the Coming Judge
summary: The psalm calls for a new song because the LORD has won a victory and made his salvation known to the nations, remembering his love and faithfulness to Israel. All the earth is summoned to shout and play lyre, harp, trumpet, and ram's horn before the King. Then the sea, the rivers, and the mountains join in, because he is coming to judge the world with righteousness.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 47
from.text: It is one of the enthronement psalms, a group (usually 47, 93, and 95 to 99) that celebrate the LORD as king.

line: A new song for the LORD's victory: all the earth shouts with lyre and horn, and the rivers clap their hands, because he is coming to judge the world with righteousness.
guide: Ask what God has done that deserves a new song from you, and let joy be loud sometimes. Let the clapping rivers remind you that the world is waiting for its King, and praise him with it.

stanzas.title: The LORD's victory revealed to the nations
All the earth, sing and play before the King
Sea, rivers, and mountains welcome the Judge

verses.t: A Psalm. Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders; His right hand and holy arm have gained Him the victory.
The LORD has proclaimed His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations.
He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth; break forth—let your cry ring out, and sing praises!
Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre, in melodious song with the harp.
With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn shout for joy before the LORD, the King.
Let the sea resound, and all that fills it, the world, and all who dwell in it.
Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains sing together for joy
before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity.
